Diagnosis:
The test failure and bug report indicate the issue occurs in the token bursting logic of PosixParser when stopAtNonOption is enabled. The current behavior does not correctly stop bursting a bundled token when a non-option character is encountered; it continues to split the token into individual options incorrectly.

Investigation of the relevant method PosixParser.burstToken(String token, boolean stopAtNonOption) shows that it iterates through each character of the token starting at index 1. For each character, if it is a defined option, it adds it to tokens. If the option expects an argument, the remainder of the token is added as an argument and the bursting breaks. Otherwise, if the character is not a defined option and stopAtNonOption is true, it calls process on the remainder of the token but does not break the loop, allowing further bursting to continue. If stopAtNonOption is false, it adds the entire token and breaks. The missing breaking after process call means bursting continues even after encountering a non-option character, defying the intended stop behavior.

The process method when called adds a "--" token and the remainder token, marking the rest as non-option arguments, but because burstToken doesn't break, subsequent characters are incorrectly fragmented into separate tokens. This matches the issue described in the report where an input like "-azb" with stopAtNonOption=true results in "-a zb -b" instead of "-a zb".

Hence, the root cause is the missing break statement after calling process(token.substring(i)) in burstToken. Adding a break after this process call would correctly stop bursting on the first non-option character encountered, which matches the expected behavior.

No other recent bug reports provide contradicting information, so the diagnosis focuses on this control flow flaw in PosixParser.burstToken.

Next steps:
The fix should be applied inside PosixParser.burstToken(String, boolean) to break the loop after calling process on the remainder token when stopAtNonOption is true and a non-option character is found. This will satisfy the test and fix the bug described.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
